cards.title: The Thumping Dryer
cards.prompt: A laundromat at midnight. One dryer has been thumping for an hour.
cards.tip: Decide whose laundry is in that dryer.

cards.title: Kitchen at the Party
cards.prompt: A kitchen during a family party. The oven timer won’t stop beeping.
cards.tip: Decide whose kitchen it is and what’s in the oven.

cards.title: Lighthouse Stairs
cards.prompt: Halfway up a lighthouse staircase. Wind whistles through a cracked window.
cards.tip: Say how many steps are left.

cards.title: Bowling Shoe Counter
cards.prompt: The shoe counter at a bowling alley. It smells of disinfectant spray.
cards.tip: Name a shoe size in your first line.

cards.title: Dentist’s Waiting Room
cards.prompt: A dentist’s waiting room. The fish tank bubbles louder than it should.
cards.tip: Waiting rooms make everyone polite. Use that.

cards.title: The Watchful Seagull
cards.prompt: A crowded beach at noon. A seagull is watching your lunch very closely.
cards.tip: Decide what’s in the lunch. The seagull already knows.

cards.title: Stuck Ferris Wheel
cards.prompt: The top of a stopped Ferris wheel. The car creaks when anyone shifts.
cards.tip: You are perfectly safe. Describe the view out loud.

cards.title: Coffee and Patience
cards.prompt: Gate 99 at 4 a.m. The carpet smells of coffee and patience.
cards.tip: Name the destination in your first two lines.

cards.title: Backstage at the Play
cards.prompt: Backstage at a school play, one minute to curtain. Dust and hairspray.
cards.tip: Name the play. Keep your voice down.

cards.title: Lost and Found
cards.prompt: A theme park lost-and-found at closing. Somewhere, a toy keeps squeaking.
cards.tip: Name one lost thing and who misses it.

cards.title: Submarine Galley
cards.prompt: The galley of a submarine. A sonar ping sounds every few seconds.
cards.tip: Cook something specific in a very small space.

cards.title: Middle of the Maze
cards.prompt: The center of a hedge maze. It smells of cut grass and sunscreen.
cards.tip: Agree early on how long you’ve been lost.

cards.title: Inside the Car Wash
cards.prompt: Inside a car wash, mid-cycle. The brushes thunder across the roof.
cards.tip: Use the noise. Each brush pass cuts someone off.

cards.title: Tomatoes in Winter
cards.prompt: A greenhouse in winter. The air is warm, wet and smells of tomatoes.
cards.tip: Name the plant you are proudest of.

cards.title: Aisle Nine
cards.prompt: A busy supermarket, aisle nine. The freezer doors hum and fog up.
cards.tip: Name exactly what is on the shelf beside you.

cards.title: The Cheese Cave
cards.prompt: A cheese cave dug into a hillside. It smells exactly as you’d fear.
cards.tip: Name a cheese. Invent one if you need to.

cards.title: The Long Escalator
cards.prompt: A very long escalator going down. Every third step squeaks.
cards.tip: Nothing to do but talk. Make the ride matter.

cards.title: The Quiet Car
cards.prompt: The quiet car of a train. Every crunch of a snack is enormous.
cards.tip: Whisper. Let the urgency grow as the voices shrink.

cards.title: Treehouse in a Storm
cards.prompt: A treehouse in a rainstorm. The roof drums, and one corner drips.
cards.tip: Decide whose treehouse it is and what it’s for.

cards.title: Balloon Basket
cards.prompt: A hot-air balloon basket. The burner roars every few seconds.
cards.tip: Name what’s below you in your first line.

cards.title: Bakery Before Dawn
cards.prompt: A bakery kitchen before dawn. Warm bread, and flour hanging in the air.
cards.tip: Name what is in the oven right now.

cards.title: Indoor Pool
cards.prompt: An indoor swimming pool. Every word echoes, and it smells of chlorine.
cards.tip: Decide early: in the water, or beside it?

cards.title: Canoe in the Fog
cards.prompt: A canoe on a foggy lake. Paddles drip; a loon calls somewhere.
cards.tip: You can only hear the shore. Describe the sounds.

cards.title: The Polite Car Alarm
cards.prompt: Level 9 of a parking garage. A car alarm chirps, politely, somewhere.
cards.tip: Say which level you thought you were on.

cards.title: Petting Zoo
cards.prompt: A petting zoo at feeding time. Goats bleat, and the hay itches.
cards.tip: Give one goat a name and a reputation.

cards.title: Humming in the Heat
cards.prompt: A desert rest stop at noon. The vending machine hums in the heat.
cards.tip: One thing in that machine is very important.

cards.title: Halftime Locker Room
cards.prompt: A football locker room at halftime. Cleats clatter on the wet tile floor.
cards.tip: Say the score in your first line.

cards.title: End of the Bench
cards.prompt: The far end of the bench at a basketball game. Sneakers squeak nonstop.
cards.tip: Name the player everyone is watching.

cards.title: Chalk Dust
cards.prompt: A gymnastics gym during practice. Springboards thunk, and chalk dust hangs everywhere.
cards.tip: Name the event you’re warming up for.

cards.title: The Windmill Hole
cards.prompt: Hole seven at a mini-golf course. The windmill blades creak past, slowly.
cards.tip: Say how many strokes you’re on. Be honest.

cards.title: Something Is Fizzing
cards.prompt: A middle-school science lab. Something in a beaker is fizzing, louder now.
cards.tip: Name what’s in the beaker and who mixed it.

cards.title: Under the T. Rex
cards.prompt: The dinosaur hall of a museum. Footsteps echo under a giant skeleton.
cards.tip: Share one dinosaur fact you are completely sure about.

cards.title: Spelling Bee Stage
cards.prompt: The stage at the state spelling bee. The microphone squeals if you lean in.
cards.tip: Invent the word. Nobody can say you spelled it wrong.

cards.title: Chess Clock Hall
cards.prompt: A chess tournament hall. The only sound is clocks being slapped.
cards.tip: Treat every move as enormous. Name the opening.

cards.title: Back of the Bus
cards.prompt: The back row of a school bus. Every bump bounces you off the seat.
cards.tip: Say where the bus is going and who’s missing.

cards.title: Blanket Fort
cards.prompt: A blanket fort at a sleepover, way past bedtime. Sleeping bags crinkle.
cards.tip: Decide what the fort is defending, and from whom.

cards.title: Lemonade Stand
cards.prompt: A lemonade stand on the hottest day of summer. The ice is melting fast.
cards.tip: Name your price and defend it.

cards.title: Camp Mess Hall
cards.prompt: A summer camp mess hall at breakfast. It smells of syrup and bug spray.
cards.tip: Name your cabin and its biggest rival.

cards.title: A Cut Above
cards.prompt: A busy hair salon on a Saturday. Dryers roar, and scissors snip close by.
cards.tip: Name the salon’s most famous haircut.

cards.title: Nailed It
cards.prompt: A nail salon at the mall. It smells of polish and lavender lotion.
cards.tip: Name a polish color. Give it a dramatic name.

cards.title: Sock Hop
cards.prompt: A 1950s school gym during a sock hop. The jukebox skips on every record.
cards.tip: Name the song playing, and who requested it.

cards.title: Roller Disco Night
cards.prompt: A roller rink on disco night. Wheels whir, and the music thumps.
cards.tip: Decide early who can skate and who can’t.

cards.title: Be Kind, Rewind
cards.prompt: A video rental store on Friday night. It smells of popcorn and old carpet.
cards.tip: Champion one movie like your weekend depends on it.

cards.title: Live on Air, 1947
cards.prompt: A 1940s radio studio, live on air. The big clock ticks loudly.
cards.tip: Name the program, and what happens after the break.

cards.title: The Hole Story
cards.prompt: A donut shop after the big game. The fryer sizzles; it smells of sugar.
cards.tip: Name the strangest donut on the menu.

cards.title: Oh My Gourd
cards.prompt: A pumpkin patch in October. Leaves crunch, and the hay wagon rattles past.
cards.tip: Decide which pumpkin is the one, and why.

cards.title: Drawbridge Rush Hour
cards.prompt: A castle drawbridge at morning rush hour. Chains clank, and cart wheels rumble.
cards.tip: Treat the fairy-tale stuff like an ordinary commute.

cards.title: Cruise Ship Buffet
cards.prompt: A cruise ship buffet at the lunch rush. The floor sways, just a little.
cards.tip: Name what’s on your plate. Then name what’s next.

cards.title: Everything Must Go
cards.prompt: A family yard sale on the driveway. Every box smells of mothballs.
cards.tip: Find one thing that should never be for sale.

cards.title: Band Practice
cards.prompt: A garage during band practice. The drums rattle a shelf of paint cans.
cards.tip: Name the band. Decide who writes the songs.

cards.title: Aquarium Tunnel
cards.prompt: The glass tunnel at an aquarium. Bubbles gurgle overhead, and voices go soft.
cards.tip: Something huge just swam overhead. Name it.

cards.title: Swinging Doors
cards.prompt: A Wild West saloon at noon. The doors creak, and somebody’s spurs jingle.
cards.tip: Say what’s on the menu board. It’s short.

cards.title: Stay With the Group
cards.prompt: A tour guide who needs you to stay with the group, just this once.
cards.tip: Treat one ordinary thing as a famous landmark.

cards.title: Retired Superhero
cards.prompt: A retired superhero who needs you to time the old super-speed, just once more.
cards.tip: Each run is slower. Blame the stopwatch.

cards.title: From Next Tuesday
cards.prompt: A time traveler from next Tuesday who needs you to put down that sandwich.
cards.tip: Each reason is smaller and stranger than the last.

cards.title: One More Cup
cards.prompt: A lighthouse keeper who needs you to stay for one more cup of tea.
cards.tip: Find a new, smaller reason each time.

cards.title: Very New Intern
cards.prompt: A brand-new intern who needs your approval for every tiny decision.
cards.tip: Ask permission for things nobody asks permission for.

cards.title: Before Picture Day
cards.prompt: A big brother who needs you to fix a home haircut before picture day.
cards.tip: Every fix makes it slightly worse. Stay hopeful.

cards.title: Vegetarian Dragon
cards.prompt: A dragon on a strict vegetarian diet who needs you to hide the sausages.
cards.tip: Proud of the diet. Weak near sausages.

cards.title: Forty Years Overdue
cards.prompt: A librarian who needs you to return a book that’s forty years overdue.
cards.tip: Never raise your voice. Name the book.

cards.title: Sacred Errand
cards.prompt: A knight on a sacred quest who needs you to sell one stamp. Just one.
cards.tip: Treat the small thing like a holy relic.

cards.title: Undercover Royal
cards.prompt: A royal in disguise who needs you to stop bowing. Immediately.
cards.tip: A royal habit keeps slipping out.

cards.title: Hurt GPS
cards.prompt: A hurt car GPS who needs you to take the very next turn. Please.
cards.tip: Give directions that are really life advice.

cards.title: Swap Places
cards.prompt: A twin who needs you to swap places for one afternoon.
cards.tip: Coach the details: the laugh, the friends, the secrets.

cards.title: Stay Very Calm
cards.prompt: A beekeeper who needs you to stay very, very calm right now.
cards.tip: Speak softly and slowly. Never quite say why.

cards.title: Step Back, Please
cards.prompt: A guard who needs you to step back from the rope. Further. No, further.
cards.tip: Treat every inch as a serious rule.

cards.title: Pigeon With a Speech
cards.prompt: A pigeon who needs you to share your fries, and has prepared a speech.
cards.tip: Use big formal words. Never forget the fries.

cards.title: Imaginary Friend
cards.prompt: An imaginary friend who needs you to set an extra place at dinner.
cards.tip: Be specific about where you sit and what you eat.

cards.title: Robot Vacuum
cards.prompt: A robot vacuum who needs you to lift your feet. Again.
cards.tip: Stay flat and patient. Report every crumb.

cards.title: The Last Potato
cards.prompt: A grandparent who needs you to take the last potato, no arguments.
cards.tip: Every refusal earns a better reason to eat it.

cards.title: Short on Teeth
cards.prompt: A tooth fairy, short on stock this week, who needs to borrow one of your teeth.
cards.tip: Treat it like a perfectly normal business loan.

cards.title: Already Like That
cards.prompt: A younger sibling who needs you to say the vase was already like that.
cards.tip: Add one detail each time. It gets worse.

cards.title: Name the Ingredient
cards.prompt: A chef who needs you to taste the soup and name the secret ingredient.
cards.tip: React to every wrong guess like it’s a clue.

cards.title: Check Your Pockets
cards.prompt: A magician mid-trick who needs you to check your pockets, quickly.
cards.tip: Name what was supposed to appear.

cards.title: Forgot the Password
cards.prompt: A spy who forgot the password and needs you to say it first.
cards.tip: Every password tried is nearly right. Say what’s missing.

cards.title: Waffle Ticket
cards.prompt: A ticket inspector who needs you to explain why your ticket is a waffle.
cards.tip: Take the waffle completely seriously.

cards.title: Discovered It
cards.prompt: An old-fashioned explorer who needs you to sign a paper saying this place was undiscovered.
cards.tip: Name and claim each thing you find.

cards.title: Rematch
cards.prompt: A chess grandmaster who just lost and needs you to play again. Right now.
cards.tip: Blame the board, the light, the chair. Never yourself.

cards.title: Apology Coach
cards.prompt: A coach who needs you to give one hundred and ten percent at saying sorry.
cards.tip: Coach every word. Demand one more rep.

cards.title: Sign In, Please
cards.prompt: A security guard who needs you to sign in. Twice.
cards.tip: Follow the rules exactly. Apologize for nothing.

cards.title: Needy Houseplant
cards.prompt: A houseplant who needs you to find a sunnier spot. Not that one.
cards.tip: Every new spot is almost right.

cards.title: This Lovely Box
cards.prompt: A real-estate agent who needs you to buy this cardboard box today.
cards.tip: Name one feature of the box per line.

cards.title: Stuck in the Suit
cards.prompt: A team mascot, stuck in the suit since Tuesday, who needs you to find the zipper.
cards.tip: Stay cheerful. Mascots never break character.

cards.title: Nine Seasons
cards.prompt: A benchwarmer of nine seasons who needs you to fake a very small injury.
cards.tip: Suggest smaller and smaller injuries. Stay polite.

cards.title: For a Seven
cards.prompt: An Olympic judge who needs you to try that entrance again. For a seven.
cards.tip: Score everything out of ten. Explain each deduction.

cards.title: Attempt Ninety-One
cards.prompt: A skateboarder on attempt ninety-one who needs you to keep filming. This is the one.
cards.tip: Describe each fall in one calm sentence.

cards.title: Tutorial First
cards.prompt: A final boss who needs you to go back and finish the tutorial first.
cards.tip: Sound enormous. Care deeply about the basics.

cards.title: Top Shelf
cards.prompt: A tyrannosaurus who needs you to reach the top shelf, and would rather not discuss why.
cards.tip: Stay dignified. Never mention the arms yourself.

cards.title: Lab Partner
cards.prompt: A lab partner who needs you to write up the experiment. Leave out the foam.
cards.tip: Add one detail about the experiment each line.

cards.title: Tab at the Stand
cards.prompt: A lemonade stand owner, age nine, who needs you to settle your tab. With interest.
cards.tip: Quote exact amounts, down to the cent.

cards.title: Substitute Teacher
cards.prompt: A substitute teacher who needs you to sit in your actual seat this time.
cards.tip: Stay polite. Check the seating chart every line.

cards.title: Class Hamster
cards.prompt: A class hamster who needs you to leave the cage door open. By accident.
cards.tip: Plan it like a heist. Keep your voice down.

cards.title: The Dog Did It
cards.prompt: A dog who ate the homework and needs you to take the blame for once.
cards.tip: Be loyal, be sorry, and mention the taste.

cards.title: Stylist With a Vision
cards.prompt: A hairstylist with a vision who needs you to sit still and not ask questions.
cards.tip: Describe the vision in pieces. Never the whole.

cards.title: Four Hundred Colors
cards.prompt: A nail artist who needs you to pick a color. There are four hundred.
cards.tip: Name each color like a paint chip.

cards.title: The Lucky Sweater
cards.prompt: A personal stylist who needs you to give up the lucky sweater. It has done enough.
cards.tip: Be kind about the sweater. Honor its service.

cards.title: Say Cheese
cards.prompt: A school photographer who needs you to say cheese like it means something.
cards.tip: Direct like a film director. One note per line.

cards.title: Never Learned to Stop
cards.prompt: A waiter on roller skates who can’t stop and needs you to order quickly.
cards.tip: You pass the table every few seconds. Use that.

cards.title: Hooves First
cards.prompt: An old-time radio actor who needs you to do the sound effects. Hooves first.
cards.tip: Narrate grandly, then leave a gap for the sound.

cards.title: If Convenient
cards.prompt: A polite sheriff who needs you to leave town by sundown, if that works.
cards.tip: Threaten nothing. Offer to help pack.

cards.title: One Perfect Joke
cards.prompt: A dad with one perfect joke who needs you to mention being hungry.
cards.tip: Steer every topic toward food. Then: “Hi, Hungry, I’m Dad.”

cards.title: Outstanding
cards.prompt: A scarecrow who needs you to cover the field for one lunch break.
cards.tip: Explain the job: stand still, be outstanding in the field.

cards.title: Orange You Glad
cards.prompt: A fruit seller who needs you to try a sample, and has a pun per fruit.
cards.tip: Grape, pear, berry, peach: let the fruit do the work.

cards.title: Troll Toll
cards.prompt: A bridge troll who needs you to pay the toll: one decent joke.
cards.tip: Groan at every joke, then ask for a better one.

cards.title: A Small Gasp
cards.prompt: A shy ghost who needs you to gasp. Even a small one would help.
cards.tip: Try gentle boos. Apologize after each one.

cards.title: Feed the Goldfish
cards.prompt: A supervillain who needs you to feed the goldfish during the world takeover. Twice a day.
cards.tip: Big plans, small instructions. Name the goldfish.

cards.title: Open the Door
cards.prompt: A cat who needs you to open the door, and has no plans to go through.
cards.tip: Explain nothing. Want it more each line.

cards.title: One Triangle Short
cards.prompt: A garage band singer who needs you to join on triangle. The triangle is vital.
cards.tip: Pitch the triangle part like a record deal.

cards.title: Batch Nine
cards.prompt: A chili cook who needs you to taste batch nine. Batch eight ate the spoon.
cards.tip: Describe each earlier batch by what it did.

cards.title: Just in Case
cards.prompt: A parent who needs you to bring a jacket, just in case. In July.
cards.tip: Each reason is a weather story from years ago.

cards.title: Eleven, to Be Safe
cards.prompt: A fairy godparent who needs you to be home by midnight. Eleven, to be safe.
cards.tip: Each new curfew is earlier. Blame the pumpkin.

cards.title: Chicken or Pasta
cards.prompt: A flight attendant who needs you to choose: chicken or pasta. The pasta is gone.
cards.tip: Keep offering the choice. Keep smiling.

cards.title: Yes, And
cards.prompt: Every line starts with “Yes, and…” then adds one new detail.
cards.tip: Yes to the facts, not the want. Keep it hard.

cards.title: Nature Documentary
cards.prompt: Talk about each other in a hushed nature-documentary voice, like rare animals.
cards.tip: Be amazed by small habits. Keep it hushed.

cards.title: Because
cards.prompt: Every line includes the word “because.” Give a reason for everything.
cards.tip: The stranger the reason, the more seriously you say it.

cards.title: Name It Exactly
cards.prompt: Never say “thing” or “stuff.” Every object gets an exact name.
cards.tip: Not “a drink”: “warm orange juice, extra pulp.”

cards.title: Very Important Partner
cards.prompt: Everyone treats the Partner like the most important person in the world.
cards.tip: Partner: accept the attention. Don’t brush it off.

cards.title: Borrow a Word
cards.prompt: Start each line with any word the other person just said.
cards.tip: Take the word you like best, not the easiest.
cards.cue: Start with one of their words

cards.title: Catch the Mood
cards.prompt: Each line picks up the other person’s feeling and makes it bigger.
cards.tip: Bigger, not louder. Name the feeling once.
cards.cue: Catch the feeling, make it bigger

cards.title: First Time Ever
cards.prompt: Everything in this scene is happening for the very first time in history.
cards.tip: Be amazed by ordinary things, like doors.

cards.title: Questions Only
cards.prompt: Every line must be a question. The scene still has to move.
cards.tip: A question can smuggle in a new fact.

cards.title: Last Word First
cards.prompt: Start each line with the last word the other person said.
cards.tip: You can’t plan ahead. You have to listen.

cards.title: Three Words
cards.prompt: Every line is exactly three words long.
cards.tip: Three words can still accept and build.

cards.title: Film Noir
cards.prompt: Talk like a gloomy old detective film. Short sentences. Rain. Regret.
cards.tip: Describe ordinary things as if they’re hiding something.

cards.title: Polite Fury
cards.prompt: Everyone is furious and perfectly polite. Nobody raises their voice.
cards.tip: Be furious at the situation, never at each other.

cards.title: After You
cards.prompt: Both of you keep trying to be the least important person here.
cards.tip: Lower yourself kindly. Lift the other person up.

cards.title: Alphabet Scene
cards.prompt: Each line starts with the next letter of the alphabet, starting from A.
cards.tip: Names and sounds count. “X-ray!” is fine.

cards.title: Bring It Back
cards.prompt: Every line must mention something already said in this scene.
cards.tip: The oldest detail makes the best callback.

cards.title: Scoreboard
cards.prompt: End every line by announcing the score, as if this were a game.
cards.tip: Score whatever just happened. Scores can go down, too.

cards.title: Fun Fact
cards.prompt: Every line includes a fact, said with complete confidence.
cards.tip: Facts can be invented. Confidence cannot.

cards.title: Top That
cards.prompt: Each line tops the last one: bigger, better, more impressive.
cards.tip: Top the story, not the person. Bigger, not louder.

cards.title: Name That Shade
cards.prompt: Every line names a color, and plain ones don’t count. Invent the shade.
cards.tip: Not “yellow”: “school-bus yellow, slightly faded.”

cards.title: Radio Drama
cards.prompt: Make every sound effect with your voice, like an old radio play.
cards.tip: Doors creak, feet clop. Make the noise, then keep going.

cards.title: But Wait, There’s More
cards.prompt: Every line sells something, like a late-night TV ad.
cards.tip: Opener: sell the want. Partner: sell your reason for refusing.

cards.title: Compliment Everything
cards.prompt: Every line contains a compliment, especially when you disagree.
cards.tip: Refuse kindly. Kindness doesn’t mean giving in.

cards.title: Animal Habit
cards.prompt: Each of you has one animal habit that keeps getting stronger.
cards.tip: Pick a habit you can hear: sniffing, humming, hoarding snacks.

cards.title: Pun Intended
cards.prompt: Sneak in a pun whenever you can. The other person must groan.
cards.tip: Steal a word from their line and twist it.

cards.title: Rhyme Time
cards.prompt: Rhyme the end of their line, then add a fresh line to rhyme.
cards.tip: End your new line on an easy word.
cards.cue: Rhyme theirs, add a new one

cards.title: Fast-Talking Picture
cards.prompt: Talk like an old black-and-white comedy: fast, snappy and terribly polite.
cards.tip: Call everyone “pal” or “chief.” Never slow down.

cards.title: Tiny Tragedies
cards.prompt: Overreact to anything small. Shrug off anything huge.
cards.tip: A dropped fry is a disaster. A flood is fine.
cards.cue: Small is huge, huge is small

cards.title: Small Confessions
cards.prompt: Every line confesses one small, harmless secret your character has been keeping.
cards.tip: Small and specific: “I’ve never finished a crossword.”

cards.title: An Hour Later
cards.prompt: Start every line with “One hour later…” and say what changed.
cards.tip: The want survives every hour. It just gets harder.

cards.title: Our Hero
cards.prompt: Speak about yourself in the third person, like a storybook hero.
cards.tip: Use your name: “Brave Ana refuses the broccoli.”

cards.title: New Rule
cards.prompt: Every line announces a new rule for this place. Everyone obeys it instantly.
cards.tip: Obey their rule first, then top it with yours.

cards.title: Bring an Umbrella
cards.prompt: It starts raining indoors. Just a light, steady drizzle.
cards.tip: Don’t stop the scene. Carry on, wetter.

cards.title: Feeling Light
cards.prompt: Gravity is suddenly half as strong as it was a moment ago.
cards.tip: Play it with voices: say what starts floating.

cards.title: Big Day
cards.prompt: The Partner has just had the best news of their life.
cards.tip: Partner: say the news out loud, straight away.

cards.title: The Last One Left
cards.prompt: Whatever the Opener wants is suddenly the last one in the world.
cards.tip: Make it rarer, not easier.

cards.title: Hidden Talent
cards.prompt: The Opener is secretly a world champion at something very small.
cards.tip: Name the tiny sport. Let it help.

cards.title: Change of Command
cards.prompt: Whoever was in charge has just been demoted. The other is promoted.
cards.tip: Play the new pecking order immediately.

cards.title: Honk
cards.prompt: A goose has gotten in. Nobody knows whose it is.
cards.tip: Someone on deck can walk on as the owner.

cards.title: Pitch Black
cards.prompt: The lights go out. The Partner has a very small flashlight.
cards.tip: Describe what you can hear and feel.

cards.title: No Cake
cards.prompt: It is the Partner’s birthday today, and everyone forgot.
cards.tip: Make it up to them with whatever is in reach.

cards.title: Sixty Seconds
cards.prompt: A health inspector arrives in exactly one minute.
cards.tip: Hide or fix one thing, out loud.

cards.title: The Movers
cards.prompt: Movers arrive and start carrying this whole place away, piece by piece.
cards.tip: Someone on deck can walk on as a mover.

cards.title: Special Delivery
cards.prompt: A package arrives for the Partner. It’s warm and smells of cinnamon.
cards.tip: Partner: open it in words. Name what’s inside.

cards.title: Signs of Trouble
cards.prompt: Every sign in this place turns out to be a pun.
cards.tip: Read one sign out loud, then carry on.

cards.title: Flag on the Play
cards.prompt: A referee walks in, blows the whistle, and calls a foul on the Opener.
cards.tip: Decide what the foul was. Take the penalty seriously.

cards.title: Slight Sway
cards.prompt: This whole place turns out to be on a boat. It always has been.
cards.tip: Mention the sway. Carry on, at sea.

cards.title: On This Spot
cards.prompt: A plaque is unveiled: something historic once happened on this exact spot.
cards.tip: Decide what happened here. Treat the spot with respect.

cards.title: One Life Left
cards.prompt: It’s all a video game. The Partner is down to one life.
cards.tip: Partner: play it careful. Everyone protect that life.

cards.title: Buddy System
cards.prompt: Thirty second-graders arrive on a field trip. All of them have questions.
cards.tip: On deck: walk on as a kid with a question.

cards.title: House Rules
cards.prompt: The floor is now officially lava. Furniture is fine.
cards.tip: Say what you are standing on. Keep the scene going.

cards.title: Fashion Week
cards.prompt: A runway opens up right through the middle of this place. Models keep coming.
cards.tip: Announce what each of you is wearing.

cards.title: Old Movie
cards.prompt: The whole world turns black and white. Only one thing keeps its color.
cards.tip: Name the one thing in color. It matters now.

cards.prompt: A disco ball lowers, and the floor lights up wherever the Opener steps.
cards.tip: Say where you step. The lights give you away.

cards.title: Loose Dad
cards.prompt: A dad wanders in. Nobody’s dad in particular. He has jokes.
cards.tip: Someone on deck can walk on as the dad.

cards.title: Chosen
cards.prompt: A cat has fallen asleep on the Partner. The Partner cannot possibly move.
cards.tip: Partner: stay put. Solve everything from where you are.

cards.title: One-Word Story
cards.prompt: Tell a story one word each, around the group. End with “The end.”
cards.tip: Say the first word you can picture.

seeds: The Town Where It Only Rained on Tuesdays

cards.title: Good News, Bad News
cards.prompt: Swing a story between “Fortunately” and “Unfortunately,” one line each.
cards.tip: “Unfortunately” complicates. It never deletes the last fact.

seeds: We left the house on time.
The map says there’s a shortcut.
The car radio only plays one song.
The dog learned to open doors.

cards.title: The Expert
cards.prompt: One player is the world’s leading expert. Everyone else asks questions.
cards.tip: No wrong answers. Only answers said with confidence.

seeds: the invention of the left turn
the secret life of traffic cones

cards.title: Same Line, New Feeling
cards.prompt: Everyone says the same ordinary line, each in a new feeling.
cards.tip: The words stay the same. Only the feeling changes.

cards.title: Half-Life
cards.prompt: Together, tell a tiny story in 60 seconds. Retell it in 30, then 15.
cards.tip: Keep the best moments. Drop everything else.

seeds: The day the map blew away
The last seat on the bus

cards.title: Story Spine
cards.prompt: Build a story together, one step of the spine per player.
cards.tip: Each step changes something for the same character.

seeds: a town with one traffic light

cards.title: Three Things
cards.prompt: Hear a category. Each player lists three of them, fast, in turn.
cards.tip: Speed beats accuracy. Celebrate every answer, even wrong ones.

seeds: things a pirate keeps in a lunchbox
things in a wizard’s glove compartment
rules at a dragon’s birthday party

cards.title: New Choice
cards.prompt: One player tells a story. Anyone calls “New choice” and the last detail changes.
cards.tip: Teller: replace the detail instantly. Never argue with it.

seeds: My first day driving the school bus
The time I won the county fair
My job at the world’s smallest café
How I lost the family recipe

cards.title: Freeze and Swap
cards.prompt: Two players act. Anyone calls “Freeze,” takes one player’s pose, and starts fresh.
cards.tip: Let the frozen pose suggest the new scene.

cards.title: The Mirror
cards.prompt: Pairs face each other. One leads slow moves; the other copies exactly. Swap.
cards.tip: Move slowly enough that nobody can tell who leads.

cards.title: Advice Line
cards.prompt: A late-night radio advice hour. Callers bring tiny problems. Hosts answer seriously.
cards.tip: Treat the smallest problem like a life decision.

seeds: My parrot only repeats my mistakes.
I can’t choose a favorite spoon.
I said “you too” when the waiter said “enjoy your meal.”
My neighbor’s rooster crows at 3 a.m.
I always pick the slowest line.

cards.title: Human Machine
cards.prompt: One by one, join a machine with a repeating sound and movement.
cards.tip: Connect to someone already moving. Keep your rhythm.

seeds: a machine that walks the dog

cards.title: Pun-Off
cards.prompt: Hear a topic. Take turns making puns about it until the group runs dry.
cards.tip: Groans count as applause. Pass if you’re stuck.

cards.title: Finish the Dad Joke
cards.prompt: Hear a dad-joke question. Each player invents a punchline. Groan generously.
cards.tip: Pause before the punchline. Deliver it like it’s brilliant.

seeds: Why did the pancake join the band?
What do you call a sleepy pizza?
Why did the calendar look nervous?
Why did the cloud get grounded?
What do you call a cow that plays the trumpet?
Why did the broom get a promotion?
Why did the spoon go to the doctor?

cards.title: The Pep Talk
cards.prompt: Build a coach’s fiery pep talk for a tiny contest, one line each.
cards.tip: Treat the tiny contest like the championship game.

seeds: choosing a restaurant in under an hour
carrying all the groceries in one trip

cards.title: Instant Replay
cards.prompt: Two players replay a sports moment in slow motion. A third narrates it.
cards.tip: Needs three: two move, one narrates. Swap roles each replay.

seeds: a close call at home plate
a golf ball heading for the pond

cards.title: Define That Word
cards.prompt: One player hears a made-up word. Everyone else asks what it means.
cards.tip: Answer like a dictionary: calm, sure and very detailed.

cards.title: Explain It to 1955
cards.prompt: One player is visiting from 1955. Others explain a modern thing to them.
cards.tip: 1955 asks practical questions. “But where does the cord go?”

cards.title: Excuses, Excuses
cards.prompt: Hear a problem. Each player offers a better excuse than the last.
cards.tip: Each excuse must be more specific, not just bigger.

seeds: You’re twenty minutes late to practice.
The dog is wearing your sweater.
You missed the school bus. Again.
The goldfish has a new name.

cards.title: Dress the Part
cards.prompt: Hear an unusual occasion. Each player adds one piece to the perfect outfit.
cards.tip: Build on the last piece. Name its color and fabric.

seeds: a family reunion at a water park
accepting a trophy for third place
dinner with a very formal grandparent

cards.title: Mixtape
cards.prompt: Make a mixtape for an occasion. Each player invents one song title.
cards.tip: Connect your song to the last one. Name the band.

seeds: waiting for the pizza to arrive
a road trip with a very old cat
the slowest elevator in the world

cards.title: Fairy Tale, Remixed
cards.prompt: Retell a fairy tale with one change, a sentence each. Keep the change alive.
cards.tip: Keep the famous moments. Let the change wreck them.

seeds: Goldilocks, but she’s a building inspector
The Three Little Pigs, but the wolf has allergies
Jack and the Beanstalk, but the giant is extremely polite
Little Red Riding Hood, but Grandma is training for a marathon
The Tortoise and the Hare, with a very strict referee
Rumpelstiltskin, but he just wants help with spelling
Hansel and Gretel, but the house is made of vegetables

cards.title: Chef’s Special
cards.prompt: Invent a dish together, one ingredient each. The last player reviews it.
cards.tip: Review it like a famous critic: one bite, big opinions.

seeds: a halftime snack for the losing team
a birthday cake for a dog
a snack for a tired knight
dinner when the power is out

cards.title: Brand-New Holiday
cards.prompt: Invent a new holiday together. Each player adds one tradition.
cards.tip: Each tradition builds on the last: a food, a song, a rule.

seeds: Take Your Parent to School Day
the Night of a Thousand Snacks

cards.title: World’s Largest Spoon
cards.prompt: You pull up beside the World’s Largest Spoon. It gleams, and it’s slightly bent.
cards.tip: Decide who bent it.

cards.title: Aunt Dot’s Driveway
cards.prompt: You pull into Aunt Dot’s driveway. The porch light is already on.
cards.tip: Greet her with the souvenir. She has questions.

cards.title: Leaning Water Tower
cards.prompt: You arrive at the Leaning Water Tower. The tourists all lean the other way.
cards.tip: Bring back the souvenir in your first three lines.

cards.title: Summit of Mount Average
cards.prompt: You reach the summit of Mount Average. It is exactly as tall as expected.
cards.tip: Make the souvenir the reason the climb was worth it.

cards.title: Sandwich Hall of Fame
cards.prompt: The doors open on the Sandwich Hall of Fame. It smells like a picnic.
cards.tip: Name one famous sandwich and why it’s famous.

cards.title: The Moon’s Gift Shop
cards.prompt: The rocket door opens on the Moon’s only gift shop. A little bell jingles.
cards.tip: The souvenir might be for sale here. Or priceless.

cards.title: Starlight Drive-In
cards.prompt: You pull into the Starlight Drive-In. The speaker crackles; the previews are starting.
cards.tip: Bring back the souvenir before the movie starts.

cards.title: Hall of Participation
cards.prompt: You arrive at the Hall of Participation. Every trophy is the same size.
cards.tip: Find the trophy with your name. Say what for.

cards.title: Museum of Close Guesses
cards.prompt: You reach the Museum of Close Guesses. Admission is roughly five dollars.
cards.tip: Name one exhibit and what it nearly got right.

cards.title: Pier Pressure
cards.prompt: You walk out onto Pier Pressure. Everyone here insists you try the fudge.
cards.tip: Let the pressure build. The souvenir is how you escape.

cards.title: Thousand-Hat Palace
cards.prompt: You arrive at the Thousand-Hat Palace. One hat was saved for you.
cards.tip: Describe your hat. Trade the souvenir for it, or don’t.

cards.title: North Pole, Off-Season
cards.prompt: You reach the North Pole in July. The workshop is closed for inventory.
cards.tip: Find an elf on break. Offer the souvenir.
